title: For g>L>=0, psi-class intersection numbers with the first n-2 exponents summing to at most L satisfy the explicit uniform lower bound lambda(g,L) times the double-factorial approximation
author: Vincent Delecroix; Elise Goujard; Peter Zograf; Anton Zorich
source_title: Uniform Lower Bound for Intersection Numbers of psi-Classes
difficulty_reason: The central obligation is to maintain an explicit multiplicative error bound uniformly in the number and distribution of descendant exponents. The proof builds compatible defects for the string, dilaton and Virasoro recursions and uses a coupled induction on the small-exponent sum and the number of zero entries, with separate genus-lowering terms. This is a substantive moduli-space intersection-number estimate, beyond evaluating a few standard correlators or applying the recursion mechanically.
source_version: Official SIGMA 16 (2020) article 086, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2020.086; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: The complete new Section2 proof was read, including the three normalized recursion-defect calculations, base two-correlator estimates credited to prior [7], the positivity discarded in the Virasoro splitting term, all branches of Proposition16 and the final genus/small-sum induction. The source convention for n=1,2 and the exact lambda product are included. The general asymptotic conjecture and later Aggarwal theorem are not selected; the asymptotic corollary is not an extra counted claim. Native source confirms the Corollary15 restriction is 3g/2, which the extracted fraction order could obscure.

statement_scope: Exactly Theorem5: integers g>L>=0, n>=1, nonnegative ordered d_i with sum d_i=3g-3+n and, for n>=3, sum of first n-2 d_i<=L; n=1,2 use the explicit unrestricted Pi_L conventions. The intersection number is at least lambda(g,L)*(6g-5+2n)!!/(product_i(2d_i+1)!!*g!*24^g), where lambda(g,L)=product_{i=0}^{L-1}(1-1/(6(g-i)+1))*(1-2/(6(g-L)-1)); the empty product for L=0 is specified. The result is a lower bound, not a two-sided uniform asymptotic theorem.
editorial_warning: Editorial source notice: in Proposition16’s k=0 branch (PDF p.10), the prose calls its displayed (2g-2+n) recursion the “string equation (2)”; the printed factor and earlier Lemma11 identify it as the dilaton equation. A later explanation writes epsilon(1,d) for the displayed epsilon(k+1,d). The unchanged formulas and explicit branch definitions determine the intended references; these are local prose slips rather than replacements of the argument.
